raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

This PR adds an opt-in mode to the b12x MoE backend: `VLLM_B12X_MOE_MXFP4_CSF=1`. In this mode, eligible W4A8 MXFP4 layers keep their E8M0 block scales in a compressed scale format (CSF) in GPU memory. On GLM-5.3-Flash with TP2, each rank uses 3.53 GiB less memory, and the KV cache holds 30.6% more tokens.

Depends on #65233. The first two commits are that PR. Review only the last commit.

## Claims

- When the switch is off, vLLM does not change.
- The mode uses the pinned `flashinfer-python==0.7.2.post1`. No new dependency is necessary.
- Ineligible layers keep uncompressed scales, and vLLM shows a warning.

## Validation

GLM-5.3-Flash, mixed MXFP4, TP2 on two DGX Spark nodes (GB10, SM121). Decode: 1,024 input and 256 output tokens. GSM8K: first 256 questions, 5-shot, temperature 0.

| | Switch off | Switch on |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Model memory per rank | 83.55 GiB | 80.02 GiB |
| KV cache | 629,418 tokens | 821,930 tokens |
| Output tokens/s, concurrency 1 / 4 / 8 | 16.32 / 43.48 / 63.76 | 16.22 / 42.09 / 61.21 |
| GSM8K | 247 / 256 | 248 / 256 |

`pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_b12x.py` passes on GB10. New tests cover the encoder, the eligibility rules, scale and output equality with uncompressed layers, and generation through `vllm_runner`.

## Details

- vLLM encodes the scales at load (`quantization/utils/mxfp4_csf.py`). The checkpoint does not change.
- FlashInfer expands the scales of the routed experts into one shared buffer per layer shape before each call. This costs 3% to 4% throughput at concurrency 4 and 8 with the pinned version. The b12x backend does not support expert parallelism or all-to-all kernels, so the layers run one at a time.
- With the switch on, all eligible layers use the prepared execution path of FlashInfer. GLM-5.3-Flash at TP2 (per-rank intermediate size 512) uses this path.
- Eligibility: gated SiLU experts, MXFP8 activations, hidden size a multiple of 256 (at most 7936), per-rank intermediate size a multiple of 64 (at most 8128). Intermediate sizes of 64 modulo 128 also need BF16 input.
- Weight reloading is not supported in this mode.

Replaces #64828, which depended on other open PRs.

-not support the model configuration. Set `VLLM_B12X_MOE_FP4_FORCE_A16=1` to
-force BF16 activations for either FP4 weight format.
+not support the model configuration. W4A8 MXFP4 layers with an intermediate size
+of 64 modulo 128 use the native prepared execution path of FlashInfer. Set
+`VLLM_B12X_MOE_FP4_FORCE_A16=1` to force BF16 activations for either FP4 weight
+format.
+
+## Compressed MXFP4 expert scales
+
+Set `VLLM_B12X_MOE_MXFP4_CSF=1` with `--moe-backend b12x` to keep eligible
+MXFP4 expert block scales in a compressed scale format (CSF) in GPU memory. This option is disabled by
+default. It needs a b12x installation that exposes `Mxfp4CsfWeights`, such as
+FlashInfer's experimental b12x package. An older standalone b12x package can
+lack this API.
+
+```bash
+VLLM_B12X_MOE_MXFP4_CSF=1 vllm serve <MXFP4-model> --moe-backend b12x
+```
+
+Each tensor-parallel rank encodes its scales without loss after it loads its
+shard. FlashInfer selects the scale representation from the weight geometry.
+If the prepared execution plan supports inline decoding, the GEMM kernels read
+the compressed scales directly. Other plans expand the scales of the routed
+experts into shared buffers before the MoE call. vLLM prepares and caches this
+selection before CUDA graph capture. Activation precision does not change.
+The selected FlashInfer kernels set the GEMM layouts and intermediate rounding.
+
+Compression reduces the resident scale memory for compressible checkpoints.
+It adds encoding time at load. The compression ratio and the inference overhead
+depend on the prepared representation and the batch shape. Inline storage can
+be larger than the canonical compressed payload.
+
+This path requires MXFP8 activations and gated experts. The hidden size must
+be a multiple of 256 and at most 7936. The per-rank intermediate size must be a
+multiple of 64 and at most 8128. Compact layouts (an intermediate size of 64
+modulo 128) require SiLU and BF16 input and output. This feature requires a
+FlashInfer version with the prepared execution API, such as the pinned
+flashinfer-python 0.7.2.post1.
+
+Other shapes keep uncompressed scales and emit a warning. BF16 activation
+backends (including `VLLM_B12X_MOE_FP4_FORCE_A16=1`) and packages without the
+CSF or prepared execution API do the same.
+
+Resident CSF layers do not support weight reloading. Each distinct layer shape
+keeps one uncompressed scale buffer. Layers of that shape share it during
+execution. The b12x MoE backend does not support expert parallelism or
+all-to-all kernels, so layers run one at a time and the shared buffer is safe.
+
+The pinned FlashInfer expands the compressed scales of the routed experts
+before each call. This can make throughput slightly lower. Newer FlashInfer
+versions can read the compressed scales inline.
 
 ## Supported Configurations

+@pytest.mark.parametrize("enforce_eager", [True, False])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("intermediate", [192, 256])
+def test_b12x_mxfp4_csf_checkpoint_loading_preserves_generation(
+    tmp_path, monkeypatch, vllm_runner, enforce_eager, intermediate
+):
+    """Loading packed weights preserves generation with one routed row per call."""
+    from safetensors.torch import save_file
+    from transformers import Qwen3MoeConfig, Qwen3MoeForCausalLM
+
+    from vllm import SamplingParams
+    from vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe import RoutedExperts
+    from vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.mxfp4 import Mxfp4MoEMethod
+
+    monkeypatch.setenv("VLLM_ALLOW_INSECURE_SERIALIZATION", "1")
+    # Compare matching GEMM layouts to isolate scale storage from arithmetic.
+    monkeypatch.setenv("B12X_W4A8_CSF_INLINE", str(int(intermediate % 128 == 64)))
+    config = Qwen3MoeConfig(
+        vocab_size=128,
+        hidden_size=256,
+        intermediate_size=256,
+        moe_intermediate_size=intermediate,
+        num_hidden_layers=2,
+        num_attention_heads=4,
+        num_key_value_heads=4,
+        head_dim=64,
+        num_experts=8,
+        num_experts_per_tok=1,
+        max_position_embeddings=64,
+    )
+    config.architectures = ["Qwen3MoeForCausalLM"]
+    with torch.device("cpu"), torch.random.fork_rng(devices=[]):
+        torch.manual_seed(29)
+        weights = {
+            name: tensor.contiguous()
+            for name, tensor in Qwen3MoeForCausalLM(config)
+            .to(torch.bfloat16)
+            .state_dict()
+            .items()
+            if ".mlp.experts." not in name
+        }
+        for index in range(2):
+            for expert in range(8):
+                for projection, rows, cols in (
+                    ("gate_proj", intermediate, 256),
+                    ("up_proj", intermediate, 256),
+                    ("down_proj", 256, intermediate),
+                ):
+                    prefix = f"model.layers.{index}.mlp.experts.{expert}.{projection}"
+                    weights[f"{prefix}.weight"] = torch.randint(
+                        256, (rows, cols // 2), dtype=torch.uint8
+                    )
+                    weights[f"{prefix}.weight_scale"] = torch.randint(
+                        118, 122, (rows, cols // 32), dtype=torch.uint8
+                    )
+    config.quantization_config = {"quant_method": "mxfp4"}
+    config.save_pretrained(tmp_path)
+    save_file(weights, str(tmp_path / "model.safetensors"))
+
+    results = []
+    for compressed in (False, True):
+        monkeypatch.setenv("VLLM_B12X_MOE_MXFP4_CSF", str(int(compressed)))
+
+        def check_resident_scales(model, compressed=compressed):
+            layers = [m for m in model.modules() if isinstance(m, RoutedExperts)]
+            assert len(layers) == 2
+            pointers = []
+            for layer in layers:
+                assert isinstance(layer.quant_method, Mxfp4MoEMethod)
+                assert (
+                    layer.quant_method.mxfp4_backend == Mxfp4MoeBackend.B12X_MXFP4_MXFP8
+                )
+                assert layer.w13_weight_scale.numel() == 0
+                assert layer.w2_weight_scale.numel() == 0
+                prepared = layer._b12x_prepared_experts
+                inline = intermediate % 128 == 64
+                assert (prepared.mxfp4_csf_inline is not None) == (
+                    compressed and inline
+                )
+                assert (prepared.mxfp4_csf is not None) == (compressed and not inline)
+                pointers.append(
+                    (
+                        prepared.w1_blockscale.data_ptr(),
+                        prepared.w2_blockscale.data_ptr(),
+                    )
+                )
+            if compressed:
+                assert pointers[0] == pointers[1]
+
+        with vllm_runner(
+            str(tmp_path),
+            dtype="bfloat16",
+            moe_backend="b12x",
+            skip_tokenizer_init=True,
+            enforce_eager=enforce_eager,
+            enable_flashinfer_autotune=False,
+            max_model_len=32,
+            max_num_seqs=1,
+            max_num_batched_tokens=32,
+            kv_cache_memory_bytes=16 << 20,
+            seed=29,
+            compilation_config={"cudagraph_capture_sizes": [1, 2, 4]},
+        ) as llm:
+            llm.apply_model(check_resident_scales)
+            completion = (
+                llm.get_llm()
+                .generate(
+                    [{"prompt_token_ids": [1]}],
+                    SamplingParams(
+                        temperature=0, max_tokens=4, ignore_eos=True, logprobs=4
+                    ),
+                )[0]
+                .outputs[0]
+            )
+            assert len(completion.token_ids) == 4
+            results.append(
+                (
+                    completion.token_ids,
+                    [
+                        {token: value.logprob for token, value in step.items()}
+                        for step in completion.logprobs
+                    ],
+                )
+            )
+    assert results[0] == results[1]
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "hidden,intermediate,activation,dtype,expected",
+    [
+        (256, 192, MoEActivation.SILU, torch.bfloat16, True),
+        (256, 256, MoEActivation.SILU, torch.bfloat16, True),
+        (4096, 1024, MoEActivation.SILU, torch.bfloat16, True),
+        (256, 224, MoEActivation.SILU, torch.bfloat16, False),
+        (8192, 192, MoEActivation.SILU, torch.bfloat16, False),
+        (256, 8192, MoEActivation.SILU, torch.bfloat16, False),
+        (256, 192, MoEActivation.SITU, torch.bfloat16, False),
+        (256, 192, MoEActivation.SILU, torch.float16, False),
+        (256, 256, MoEActivation.SITU, torch.bfloat16, True),
+        (256, 256, MoEActivation.SILU, torch.float16, True),

+        hidden_dim=hidden,
+        intermediate_size=intermediate,
+        activation=activation,
+        in_dtype=dtype,
+    )
+    has_csf = _has_b12x_csf()
+    assert mxfp4_oracle.mxfp4_backend_supports_csf_scales(

+    ) == (has_csf and expected)

+    not _has_b12x_moe() or not _has_b12x_csf(),
+    reason="requires b12x MXFP4 CSF kernels on SM120/SM121",
+)
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("intermediate", [192, 256])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("tokens,topk", [(1, 2), (3, 1), (7, 1), (64, 2)])
+@torch.inference_mode()
+def test_b12x_mxfp4_resident_scales_match_plain_scales(
+    intermediate, tokens, topk, monkeypatch, workspace_init
+):
+    """CSF preserves scales and outputs for cached live capacities and graph replays."""
+    from vllm.v1.worker.workspace import lock_workspace
+
+    monkeypatch.setenv("B12X_W4A8_CSF_INLINE", str(int(intermediate % 128 == 64)))
+    set_random_seed(29)
+    num_experts, hidden = 8, 256
+    config = make_dummy_moe_config(
+        num_experts=num_experts,
+        experts_per_token=topk,
+        hidden_dim=hidden,
+        intermediate_size=intermediate,
+    )
+    backend = Mxfp4MoeBackend.B12X_MXFP4_MXFP8
+    weights = [

+def _decode_mxfp4_csf_scales(
+    fixed: torch.Tensor, exceptions: torch.Tensor, cols: int
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Rebuild one CPU ``[rows, cols]`` E8M0 matrix from its b12x planes."""
+    if (
+        fixed.dtype != torch.uint8
+        or fixed.dim() != 2
+        or fixed.shape[0] == 0
+        or exceptions.dtype != torch.uint32
+        or not 1 <= cols <= 255
+        or fixed.shape[0] * MXFP4_CSF_ROWS * cols > 1 << 24
+    ):
+        raise ValueError("Invalid MXFP4 CSF planes")
+    row_bytes = -(-cols // 8)
+    if fixed.shape[1] != MXFP4_CSF_ROWS * (1 + row_bytes):
+        raise ValueError("MXFP4 CSF fixed plane does not match the column count")
+    rows = fixed.shape[0] * MXFP4_CSF_ROWS
+    planes = fixed.numpy()
+    bases = planes[:, :MXFP4_CSF_ROWS].reshape(rows, 1).astype(np.int16)
+    bits = np.unpackbits(
+        planes[:, MXFP4_CSF_ROWS:].reshape(rows, row_bytes), axis=1, bitorder="little"
+    )[:, :cols]
+    out = (bases + bits).reshape(-1)
+    if (out > 255).any():
+        raise ValueError("MXFP4 CSF selector exceeds the byte range")
+    out = out.astype(np.uint8)
+    words = exceptions.reshape(-1).numpy()
+    positions = words & 0xFFFFFF
+    if positions.size and (
+        positions[-1] >= rows * cols or (positions[1:] <= positions[:-1]).any()
+    ):
+        raise ValueError("CSF exception positions must be increasing and in range")
+    out[positions] = (words >> 24).astype(np.uint8)
+    return torch.from_numpy(out.reshape(rows, cols))
+
+
+def _mxfp4_scales(experts: int, rows: int, cols: int, seed: int = 0) -> np.ndarray:
+    """E8M0 bytes clustered on two neighbours, as in real checkpoints, plus outliers."""
+    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
+    shape = (experts, rows, cols)
+    raw = 118 + rng.binomial(1, 0.4, shape)
+    outliers = rng.random(shape) < 0.02
+    raw[outliers] += rng.integers(-5, 6, int(outliers.sum()))
+    return raw.astype(np.uint8)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("rows, cols", [(16, 1), (32, 7), (64, 90), (16, 255)])
+def test_mxfp4_csf_round_trips(rows, cols):
+    raw = _mxfp4_scales(3, rows, cols)
+    fixed, exceptions = encode_mxfp4_csf_scales(torch.from_numpy(raw))
+
+    row_bytes = -(-cols // 8)
+    for expert in range(3):
+        assert fixed[expert].dtype == torch.uint8
+        assert fixed[expert].shape == (rows // 16, 16 * (1 + row_bytes))
+        assert exceptions[expert].dtype == torch.uint32
+        decoded = _decode_mxfp4_csf_scales(fixed[expert], exceptions[expert], cols)
+        assert np.array_equal(decoded.numpy(), raw[expert])
+
+
+def test_mxfp4_csf_picks_the_window_with_fewest_exceptions():
+    # Every row holds only two neighbouring bytes, so no exceptions are needed,
+    # including at the top of the byte range.
+    raw = np.empty((1, 32, 10), dtype=np.uint8)
+    raw[0, :16] = [120, 121] * 5
+    raw[0, 16:] = [254, 255] * 5
+    fixed, exceptions = encode_mxfp4_csf_scales(torch.from_numpy(raw))
+    assert exceptions[0].numel() == 0
+    assert list(fixed[0][0, :16]) == [120] * 16
+    assert list(fixed[0][1, :16]) == [254] * 16
+    assert torch.equal(
+        fixed[0][0, 16:].reshape(16, 2),
+        torch.tensor([[0xAA, 0x02]], dtype=torch.uint8).expand(16, 2),
+    )
+    decoded = _decode_mxfp4_csf_scales(fixed[0], exceptions[0], 10)
+    assert np.array_equal(decoded.numpy(), raw[0])
+
+
+def test_mxfp4_csf_keeps_arbitrary_bytes_exact():
+    raw = np.random.default_rng(1).integers(0, 256, (2, 32, 33), dtype=np.uint8)

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Lossless CSF encoding of MXFP4 (E8M0) expert block scales for b12x.
+
+Each scale matrix is stored as a compact fixed plane plus a short list of
+exception words, which b12x consumes as resident compressed expert scales.
+"""
+
+import numpy as np
+import torch
+
+# MXFP4 (E8M0) scales: b12x consumes canonical planes per expert. Each 16-row
+# slab holds one base byte per row, then every row's one-bit selectors
+# (``ceil(cols / 8)`` bytes per row, low bit first); a set bit selects
+# ``base + 1`` over ``base``. Exceptions are sorted uint32 words: low 24 bits a
+# flat ``row * cols + col`` position, high 8 bits the exact scale byte.
+MXFP4_CSF_ROWS = 16
+
+
+def encode_mxfp4_csf_scales(
+    scales: torch.Tensor,
+) -> tuple[tuple[torch.Tensor, ...], tuple[torch.Tensor, ...]]:
+    """Encode ``[experts, rows, cols]`` E8M0 block scales as b12x MXFP4 planes.
+
+    A row's base is the lowest byte whose two-value window ``{base, base + 1}``
+    holds the most of the row's bytes, which minimizes exceptions. Returns each
+    expert's fixed plane (uint8) and exception words (uint32) on the CPU.
+    """
+    if scales.dim() != 3 or scales.element_size() != 1:
+        raise ValueError(
+            f"Expected [experts, rows, cols] byte scales, got {scales.shape}"
+        )
+    experts, rows, cols = scales.shape
+    if (
+        experts == 0
+        or rows == 0
+        or rows % MXFP4_CSF_ROWS
+        or not 1 <= cols <= 255
+        or rows * cols > 1 << 24
+    ):
+        raise ValueError(
+            "MXFP4 CSF needs nonempty experts, positive rows divisible by 16, "
+            "1..255 columns and at most "
+            f"2**24 scales per matrix, got {rows}x{cols}"
+        )
+    raw = scales.contiguous().view(torch.uint8).cpu().numpy()
+    row_bytes = -(-cols // 8)
+    fixed: list[torch.Tensor] = []
+    exceptions: list[torch.Tensor] = []
+    for expert in range(experts):
+        values = raw[expert]
+        keys = (np.arange(rows, dtype=np.int64)[:, None] << 8) | values
+        counts = np.bincount(keys.reshape(-1), minlength=rows << 8).reshape(rows, 256)
+        bases = (counts[:, :255] + counts[:, 1:]).argmax(1).astype(np.uint8)
+        offsets = values.astype(np.int16) - bases[:, None]
+        selected = offsets == 1
+        outliers = (offsets != 0) & ~selected
+        bits = np.packbits(selected, axis=1, bitorder="little")
+        assert bits.shape[1] == row_bytes
+        slabs = np.concatenate(
+            (
+                bases.reshape(-1, MXFP4_CSF_ROWS),
+                bits.reshape(-1, MXFP4_CSF_ROWS * row_bytes),
+            ),
+            axis=1,
+        )
+        fixed.append(torch.from_numpy(np.ascontiguousarray(slabs)))
+        positions = np.flatnonzero(outliers.reshape(-1)).astype(np.uint32)
+        words = (values.reshape(-1)[positions].astype(np.uint32) << 24) | positions
+        exceptions.append(torch.from_numpy(words.astype(np.uint32)))
+    return tuple(fixed), tuple(exceptions)
